exposure: duration of arrest at full cervical dilatation
outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: The study included 49 women who underwent cesarean section at full cervical dilatation.
finding: Persistent occiput posterior position was the only significant risk factor for poor perinatal outcome after cesarean section at full cervical dilatation, with a duration of arrest at full cervical dilatation exceeding 1.25 hours further increasing this risk.
mod_finding: Persistent occiput posterior position and a duration of arrest at full cervical dilatation longer than 1.25 hours are identified as risk factors for poor perinatal outcomes specifically after cesarean section performed at full cervical dilatation.
